title: Why are we sending all this money to Ukraine - there are problems her...
description: Why are we sending all this money to Ukraine - there are problems here? This is the question is being asked in countries. Last week in Germany I saw that a man was forced to move out of a house he  - that was renting ALONE, at a reduced rate - because officials wanted it for a family, that was thought to be from Ukraine. A TikTok from the US showed footage of homeless tent cities in California and asked why the US government wasn't taking care of Americans first.  Sending money, military and humanitarian aid to other places, is one topic, taking in displaced people is another.  Why are ultimately your taxer are being used to improve the lives of people around the world. The simple hard answer is they are doing it for YOU. Look around,  if you are doing better than others, its in your countires interest to bring that standard to other places so you can maintain your standard. It seems over simplified - but with how interconnected our world is if there is a disease in one place because it will come to you, if there are limited rights, people will try to go where they can be free, by reducing poverty or the impacts of climate change in other places they also won't affect you. There are huge differences in what motivates humanitarian aid and military aid.  But both types of aid are tied to what the counties providing them hold as important values. In most government systems there are budgets set and what is happening in the country isn’t always reflected in how the country helps on the outside.  Look at America, US voters have opted for lower taxes and less or no support for the homeless, jobless, and sick people, they approved less money for education since the 1980s and in a lot of places reject the idea of universal healthcare. Americans that are complaining about supporting Ukraine because there are problems at home often have voted for or supported the polities that created these problems.  There is also the idea that Ukrainian displaced persons in Europe, and the rest of the world, are being unfairly favoured. Structural racism is certainly at play, and so are political interests. The alignments between domestic, and political ideologies and international relations factor into this situation. Think about this,  Ukraine has a large population – 44 million people – more populous than Iraq, Syria, Libya, and Afghanistan. Ukraine is also a lot closer to Europe and easier to travel from.  In April the Kyiv Post reported that over 90% of Ukrainians wanted to return home - this number has only fluctuated a little, in month 7 of the war, with Ukrainians worried about winter temperatures are now saying, or example in a polish survey, wait until after winter to return.  That most Ukrainians don’t want to stay where ever they are differentiates them from other groups. In September, there were reports of Bot-like social media accounts that were amplifying anti-Ukraine hashtags on social media in Poland. Tiktok is probably no different, with efforts being made to question the political response to Ukraine and how Ukrainians are being treated. As Russia’s war in Ukraine continues, so does the information war on social media.  What is your response when  people ask ….
